newTheorem.statement: If an integer zero-sum coefficient vector c has no proper zero-sum coefficient subset, and A is c-free with span L, then A union (D+A) is c-free for every D > L*sum_i|c_i|. Iterating gives a certified doubling construction and an explicit cardinality-birth upper recurrence.
newTheorem.proof: Internal tuples are excluded by freeness. Every cross tuple has translated-side coefficient sum C_R!=0. Its translation term has magnitude at least D, while the residual has magnitude at most L*||c||_1, so it cannot vanish.

exactRejectionBoundary.boundary: separation-only doubling is rejected exactly when a proper translated-side coefficient subset sums to zero; its residual survives every D

compressedExplanation: Large separation kills every cross pattern unless the coefficients placed on the translated side sum to zero. Thus the coefficient subset-sum profile—not vague “large gaps”—is the exact switch between a doubling theorem and a permanent gluing obligation.
